pr.title: Read review settings from GitHub's default branch when no live session has a checkout, so CI-reviewed pull requests hear no UNREVIEWED
pr.head: 423f0d135439c5a1be11c5dbc3e10f2219267efd

summary: The watch daemon is the background process that polls every pull request a session subscribes to, and announces events such as UNREVIEWED. That event says that a ready pull request's head isn't signed off and that no session will review it. Two settings decide whether the event fires: review.ci says GitHub Actions reviews the repository's own pull requests, and review.reviewers names extra logins, such as a CI app's [bot] account, whose Projector verdicts count toward sign-off.

The daemon used to read those settings only from a checkout of the repository that a live session works in. For a repository a session watches but has no checkout of, it found neither setting. So its ready pull requests heard UNREVIEWED even though review.ci = true was committed and CI reviewed every head.

With this change, when no live checkout covers a repository, the daemon reads the .projector.toml committed on its default branch through GitHub's contents API. It layers that file under your ~/.projector.toml and caches the result per repository for 10 minutes. A live checkout still wins whenever one exists.

groups.title: Loading a committed configuration
groups.kicker: A config loader for a file that came from GitHub rather than from disk
intro: config.load walks from a checkout up to your home directory and layers each .projector.toml it finds. The daemon has no checkout to walk here, so the new load_committed builds the same Config from two layers: your user file, then the bytes GitHub returned. It reuses parse_config and layered, so overrides, user-only keys, and setting types behave the same way they do in a checkout.

files.note: Adds load_committed, which layers the user file and then the committed file's bytes.

checks.text: The user layer comes first, which is lowest precedence, matching load. The committed file's relative Source path can't equal the resolved user path, so user-only keys are still read only from your own file. Checked by reading layered.

groups.title: Reading and caching the settings in the daemon
groups.kicker: Where the daemon decides between a live checkout and GitHub
intro: Pass.settings_of fills its map from live checkouts once per pass, as before. For a repository that isn't in that map, it now asks Daemon.committed_settings, which calls gh api repos/<repo>/contents/.projector.toml with no ref, so it reads only the default branch and never a pull request's head.

The daemon keeps the result in Daemon.committed, keyed by the lowercased repository and stamped with its monotonic clock. This cache lives across passes, so a pass over many pull requests makes at most one request per repository every 10 minutes.

checks.text: The settings change which verdicts count and whether UNREVIEWED fires. A repository's committed default branch already takes write access to change, which is the same trust a checkout's committed file carries.

files.note: Adds committed_settings and its cache, factors out review_settings, and makes settings_of fall back to GitHub.

checks.text: A 404 applies only the user layer. A base64 200 is decoded and parsed. A failed call, a body that isn't JSON, a directory listing, or another encoding logs and keeps the last settings. A ConfigError or a base64 padding error is caught. Checked by reading every branch.
A live checkout's entry is in repo_settings before the GitHub fallback runs, so the checkout always wins. test_a_live_checkouts_review_settings_win_over_githubs covers this.

groups.title: Tests and documentation
groups.kicker: Fake contents API, six regression tests, and the updated reference rows
intro: The fake gh in tests/test_watch.py now serves the contents API, with a 404 when a repository commits no file. Every watch test points HOME at a scratch directory, so the runner's own ~/.projector.toml can't leak into the committed-settings layering. The new tests cover reading the settings, a 404, the 10-minute cache, a failed read, your user layer, and checkout precedence.
docs/cli.md now describes both sources in the review.reviewers and review.ci rows and in the UNREVIEWED event.

files.note: The two configuration rows and the UNREVIEWED event row now name the GitHub fallback.
